summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent pneumonias and COPD, was admitted due to increased oxygen requirements and lethargy. A chest X-ray revealed a new left lower lobe pneumonia, and she was started on IV vancomycin and Zosyn. Sputum cultures identified methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus sensitive to Bactrim. Due to loss of IV access, antibiotics were transitioned to oral linezolid and ciprofloxacin, with plans to complete a ten-day course of Bactrim at home. A concurrent urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella resistant to Bactrim was treated with a seven-day course of ciprofloxacin. The patient improved clinically, with oxygen weaned to room air during the day and 1–2 liters at night. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up instructions and completed antibiotics.
